approach: Each force equals mass times the speed change divided by the time it acts over, and the question gives no relation between the two times.

steps.text: Write each force using Newton's second law, with the speed change divided by the time each force acts.
steps.equation: F₁ = m(v − 0)/t₁, F₂ = m(0 − v)/t₂ in size

steps.text: The question states only that the particle speeds up from rest to v under F₁ and slows from v to rest under F₂. It gives no information about the times t₁ and t₂, or about the distances covered.
steps.equation: no fixed relation between t₁ and t₂

steps.text: Since t₁ and t₂ can be anything, F₂ can come out smaller than, larger than, or equal to F₁, depending on the time over which each force acts.
steps.equation: F₂ ⋛ F₁, all three are possible

final_answer.value: F₂ may be smaller than, greater than or equal to F₁

common_mistakes.text: Assuming that the same change in speed must come from the same force overlooks that the time or distance over which each force acts is not given as equal.
Assuming that slowing something down always takes a bigger push than speeding it up confuses direction of motion with the size of the force needed.
